title: Eight Divisors of Thirty
statement: Let $N$ be the number of ordered $8$-tuples $(d_1, d_2, \dots, d_8)$ such that each $d_i$ is a positive divisor of $30$ greater than $1$ (repeated values are allowed) and the product $d_1 d_2 \cdots d_8$ is a perfect square. Find the remainder when $N$ is divided by $1000$.
hints: Fix $d_1, \dots, d_7$ and look at whether the exponents of $2$, $3$ and $5$ in their product are odd or even. What does this tell you about the possible values of $d_8$?

Use recursion on the length of the tuple. Let $a_k$ be the number of $k$-tuples of allowed divisors whose product is a perfect square, and build each $(k+1)$-tuple by appending one divisor to a $k$-tuple. A product is a square exactly when every prime exponent is even, so compare the exponent parities of the $k$-tuple's product with those of the appended divisor.

Each allowed divisor has exponents $0$ or $1$ at $2$, $3$ and $5$, and is not $1$. So a $k$-tuple with non-square product can be completed to a square product in exactly one way, and a $k$-tuple with square product cannot be completed at all. Since there are $7$ allowed divisors, this gives $a_{k+1} = 7^k - a_k$ with $a_1 = 0$. Now iterate this up to $a_8$ and reduce modulo $1000$.
solution:
The allowed values are $2,3,5,6,10,15,30$. These correspond to the nonzero vectors in $\mathbb F_2^3$ (the parities of the exponents of $2,3,5$). The product is a square exactly when the vectors sum to $0$.

Let $a_k$ be the number of $k$-tuples with square product, so $a_1=0$. Given a $k$-tuple with non-zero parity vector $v$, exactly one allowed $d$ has vector $v$, and this $d$ makes the product a square. Given a $k$-tuple with parity vector $0$, the only choice of $d$ would be vector $0$, which is not allowed. So
$$a_{k+1}=7^k-a_k.$$

Then
$$a_2=7,\ a_3=42,\ a_4=301,\ a_5=2100,\ a_6=14707,\ a_7=102942,$$
$$a_8=823543-102942=720601.$$

Hence $N=720601$, and $N\equiv 601 \pmod{1000}$.
